Severity rationale: Loss of positive confirmation for one gear unit before a surface-specific landing is a significant increase in crew workload and a reduction in the margin of correct configuration; effects support MAJ-1/MAJ-2. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of gear-configuration indication — no valid gear/lock configuration status presented to the crew
fha.effAc: Crew have no valid confirmation of gear/lock state for any unit against the selected surface; the config-versus-surface comparison cannot function, so correct configuration for a paved or water landing must be established by mechanical means and procedure alone.
fha.effCrew: Substantial workload increase to establish and confirm configuration without indication (free-fall extension, external cues), with residual uncertainty at a phase where wrong configuration is consequential.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to elevated risk of a mis-configured landing until configuration is otherwise confirmed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Loss of all configuration indication on a surface-dependent amphibian could be a large or a significant reduction in margins depending on how reliably configuration can be confirmed without indication; the SDD gives a free-fall path but not the confirmability of correct configuration, so HAZ-1 vs MAJ-1 cannot be resolved without that operational input.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of water-rudder steering authority
fha.effAc: Reduced directional control authority on the water during taxi; differential thrust remains available and the water rudder is used only for water taxi, not for flight.
fha.effCrew: Position is annunciated to the crew; crew retains differential thrust for directional control on the water.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Effect is confined to water taxi (§5.13.2); differential thrust remains as directional control on the water (§5.13.3). Reduced-authority-only during a low-speed surface manoeuvring phase supports a slight increase in crew workload — MIN-2. Confirm against declared sea state and taxi handling. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of water-rudder steering
fha.effAc: No water-rudder steering; the water rudder is simplex and, with its actuator failed, can be retracted by a manual release in the aft cabin and directional control on the water reverts to differential thrust.
fha.effCrew: Crew reverts to differential thrust for directional control on the water; manual release in the aft cabin retracts the blade.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Function is used only for water taxi and a directional-control means (differential thrust) remains (§5.13.3). Loss during a low-speed surface phase with a retained control means supports a slight increase in crew workload — MIN-2. Confirm whether close-quarters mooring/manoeuvring in the declared sea state raises this. [anchor MIN-2 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous fire or overheat warning (warning presented with no true event)
fha.effAc: Detection is dual-loop AND for warning (§5.15.2), so a warning follows agreement of two loops; a false warning may prompt crew isolation actions (fuel shutoff / bus contactor open / feather) that shut down a source not in distress, reducing available propulsion or generation.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to diagnose and to execute (or withhold) the associated isolation procedure; the crew must distinguish a false warning from a real one against other cues.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false fire/overheat warning can drive isolation of a good source (turbogenerator or a propulsion unit) on a two-source powertrain, giving a significant increase in crew workload and a potential reduction in available power — MAJ-2. Confirm whether an erroneous nacelle warning leading to feather of a good unit reaches Hazardous under a worst-phase combination. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected failure to warn of a real fire, overheat or thermal-runaway event
fha.effAc: A real event in a fire zone (energy store bay, turbogenerator compartment or a nacelle) develops without warning; the crew take no isolation, containment-monitoring or feather action, allowing an uncontrolled fire/thermal-runaway to propagate within a designated fire zone.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action regarding the event; they are denied the primary means to command isolation and discharge.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to an undetected fire/thermal event; cabin/baggage smoke detection is a separate photoelectric path (§5.15.2) and may provide a late, indirect cue only for cabin-adjacent events.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected fire or thermal-runaway in a designated fire zone that develops with no crew warning and therefore no isolation/containment response can lead to loss of the airplane — CAT-1. Confirm against the store-bay containment case (containment is passive and independent of the warning) which may bound the store-bay contribution. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded primary surface motion via channel B, undetected — channel B drives a surface half without a corresponding command and the monitored cross-compare does not flag it
fha.effAc: Sustained uncommanded surface deflection on one half of a surface pair with no crew annunciation; the counter-channel and airframe oppose it but a persistent undetected mistrack degrades trajectory control and, if the deflection is toward a hardover, can produce an upset the crew cannot immediately attribute.
fha.effCrew: No alert presented; crew fly against a mistrimmed/mistracking surface without knowing the source, delaying diagnosis and correct reversion.
fha.effPax: Potential unexpected attitude/loading excursions.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect turns on how large and how sustained an undetected channel-B deflection can be with the cross-compare defeated, and on whether the opposing channel bounds it — the SDD states cross-compare is monitored and annunciated on disagreement but does not quantify the residual authority of an undetected single-channel hardover; without that the aircraft-level outcome (Major vs Hazardous) cannot be grounded.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of primary control commanding — channel A ceases to command one or more of its surface halves; the aircraft continues on channel B through the other half of each pair
fha.effAc: One half of an affected surface pair is no longer commanded; the surfaces are sized so one half of each pair is sufficient, so controlled flight continues with reduced surface authority/redundancy on the affected axis.
fha.effCrew: Transfer/degradation annunciated; crew continue on the remaining channel and manage a modest increase in workload and reduced control margin.
fha.effPax: Little or no perceptible effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Significant reduction in functional capability and redundancy on the affected axis while safe flight continues on the sufficient counter-channel half — MAJ-1. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary control commanding — channel A loses all commanding to its surface halves
fha.effAc: Channel A commands nothing; per the architecture channel B alone is sufficient to fly the aircraft through its half of each surface pair, so controlled flight continues with the loss of one of two commanding channels.
fha.effCrew: Automatic transfer to channel B is annunciated; crew fly on the single remaining channel with no redundancy on primary commanding.
fha.effPax: Little or no perceptible effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of one commanding channel with the counter-channel stated sufficient to fly the aircraft; significant reduction in redundancy/safety margin with safe flight continuing — MAJ-1. A Hazardous classification would require the loss to compromise controlled flight, which the sufficient-counter-channel claim does not support. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous primary surface command via channel B — channel B commands a surface position that does not correspond to pilot/autopilot input, crew aware
fha.effAc: One half of an affected surface pair is driven to an erroneous position; the monitored cross-compare detects the disagreement and automatic transfer removes channel B from control, after which the aircraft flies on channel A. Transient trajectory disturbance during detection/transfer.
fha.effCrew: Disagreement and transfer annunciated; crew manage a short transient and continue on the remaining channel with increased workload.
fha.effPax: Possible brief attitude transient.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detected erroneous command bounded by the monitored cross-compare and automatic transfer to the counter-channel; significant reduction in functional capability/redundancy with safe flight continuing after a transient — MAJ-1. Severity depends on the cross-compare bounding the transient before it becomes a large excursion. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded primary surface motion via channel B — channel B drives a surface half without a corresponding command, crew aware
fha.effAc: One half of an affected surface pair moves without command; the monitored cross-compare detects the disagreement between commanded and actual/counter-channel position and automatic transfer isolates channel B, after which the aircraft flies on channel A. Transient trajectory disturbance during detection/transfer.
fha.effCrew: Disagreement and transfer annunciated; crew manage a short transient and continue on the remaining channel with increased workload.
fha.effPax: Possible brief attitude transient.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detected uncommanded motion bounded by the monitored cross-compare and automatic transfer to the sufficient counter-channel; significant reduction in functional capability/redundancy with safe flight continuing after a transient — MAJ-1. Severity depends on the cross-compare bounding the deflection before it becomes a large excursion. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of standby attitude and air-data indication — no standby attitude or air-data information is available and the standby source to FCB is lost.
fha.effAc: Aircraft continues on the primary display and FCA; the independent standby reference is lost and, with it, the dissimilar air-data/attitude source that FCB reads, so a subsequent primary-source failure has no independent fallback.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain the primary picture but lose the independent means of resolving a primary/standby disagreement; workload rises and a later primary failure would leave no valid attitude/air-data reference.
fha.effPax: No immediate effect; occupants exposed to reduced margin against a subsequent primary-source loss.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on the residual capability after this loss combined with a primary-source failure and on the FCB dependence on the standby source — the SDD states independence across sensor, probe, channel and battery but does not state the aircraft-level effect of losing that redundancy alone. Cannot derive a class without the primary/standby loss combination and FCB reversion effect being characterised; leave empty pending that.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded gear actuation — one or more gear units move without a corresponding crew selection.
fha.effAc: Uncommanded gear motion places the aircraft in a configuration inconsistent with the selected surface — extension during water operations or retraction near a paved landing degrades the safe configuration for that surface; on an amphibian the correct configuration is surface-dependent.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion against the configuration/surface comparison and re-establish the correct configuration; increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to a landing/water contact in an incorrect gear configuration if the condition is not corrected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: On an amphibian, an incorrect gear configuration for the surface (gear down on water, or gear up/retracting for a paved landing) can produce a large reduction in safety margins during a critical phase; HAZ-1 anchor. Proposed pending the phase-worst assessment of gear-vs-surface mismatch consequences; confirm whether a mismatch reaches Catastrophic in any phase. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent gear extension or retraction — the gear extends or retracts in response to an erroneous or spurious command, placing it in a configuration not selected by the crew.
fha.effAc: Inadvertent extension or retraction leaves the aircraft configured wrongly for the surface being operated to — gear extended for a water landing or retracted approaching a paved surface — degrading the safe landing configuration.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the inadvertent change against the surface selection and restore the correct configuration under time pressure; increased workload in a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Occupants exposed to an incorrect-configuration surface contact if uncorrected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Same basis as SF-008-M: surface-dependent configuration on an amphibian means an inadvertent wrong-surface configuration is a large reduction in safety margins in a critical phase; HAZ-1 anchor. Proposed pending phase-worst confirmation. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of standby attitude indication — the standby attitude source presents degraded or reduced attitude information; primary attitude on the main display remains available.
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains controllable on primary attitude indication; the independent standby attitude reference is degraded, reducing the dissimilar backup available if the primary source is later lost.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain primary attitude; loss of the independent cross-check increases monitoring workload and removes one means of resolving a later primary/standby disagreement.
fha.effPax: No immediate effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With primary attitude retained, the effect is a slight reduction in the independent backup margin (standby is the redundancy, not the primary means); MIN-1 anchor. Confirm against the reversion/independence argument of §5.11 and §5.7. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of standby air-data indication — the standby air-data source presents degraded or reduced air-data information; primary air data on the main display remains available.
fha.effAc: Aircraft remains operable on primary air data; the independent standby air-data reference feeding FCB is degraded, reducing the dissimilar backup and the means to arbitrate a primary/standby disagreement.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain primary air data; loss of the independent standby air-data cross-check increases monitoring workload.
fha.effPax: No immediate effect on occupants.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Primary air data retained; effect is a slight reduction in the independent backup margin. MIN-1 anchor. Note standby feeds FCB (§5.7/§5.11) — confirm whether FCB dependence elevates this beyond Minor. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The five resource systems (EST, EGN, TMS, EL1, EL2) are excluded from the aircraft FUNCTION list and captured as resources that functions consume.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly classifies these as resources, and the modeling rule bars authoring power/energy supply as functions; without this exclusion the function list would wrongly include resource-supply behaviours.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any of these must be modelled as an aircraft function (e.g. a special-condition demands it), add corresponding functions and their FHA rows.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of EST/EGN/TMS/EL1/EL2 from the add_function set.

citations.quote: Five are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: Hull watertight integrity (HUF/HUA) is a structural property handled by structural analysis and PRA, not an aircraft-level FHA function, whereas water directional control IS a function.
assumptions.rationale: §5.12.1/5.13.1 describe both a structural retention role and a distinct water-steering behaviour; the modeling rule excludes structural support from the functional FHA but water steering is a behaviour.
assumptions.ifWrong: If flotation/watertight integrity is to be assessed functionally (plausible given the anticipated hull special condition), add a buoyancy/flotation function and route its failure conditions accordingly.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide directional control on the water function; omission of a hull-integrity function.

citations.quote: the hull as a primary structural and flotation element

assumptions.text: One level of decomposition stops at the channel/unit/display granularity the SDD resolves, not at winding-set, half-bridge or actuator level.
assumptions.rationale: The reference method requires stopping at the level the architecture resolves and where sub-functions fail independently; the SDD's independence argument lives at channel/unit level, not piece-part.
assumptions.ifWrong: If independent failure needs to be shown below channel level (e.g. dual winding sets), a further decomposition level is required, changing the sub-function count.
assumptions.usedFor: All sub-function boundaries in this decomposition.

citations.quote: Each channel alone can fly the aircraft through its own half of each surface pair

assumptions.text: The applicable §__.1309 basis is Part 23 / AC 23.1309-1E Class III as the SDD declares, not the Part 25 recorded in the project state.
assumptions.rationale: The project state certBasis is 'Part 25' but the uploaded SDD explicitly declares Part 23 normal category with AC 23.1309-1E Class III; the two conflict.
assumptions.ifWrong: The §xx.1309 references and downstream AFHA safety objectives change from Part 23 Class III targets to Part 25 transport targets.
assumptions.usedFor: All SF-001..SF-005 rows' §xx.1309 rationale framing

citations.quote: The intended certification basis is 14 CFR Part 23, normal category, at Level 4 / high-speed

assumptions.text: Loss of a single propulsion unit is a survivable degraded condition (sector continued on the remaining unit), so per-side thrust loss is a distinct failure condition from combined dual-unit loss.
assumptions.rationale: The function list gives left/right thrust separately; the SDD sizing case is continuation on one unit, which frames per-side vs combined conditions.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single-side loss were not survivable, the per-side Total-loss rows would merge conceptually with the combined SF-001+SF-002 condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 and SF-002 Total/Partial loss rows and the flagged combined condition

praData.desc: Retractable tricycle gear: twin-wheel nose unit in zone 110, single-wheel main units in the nacelle bays (zone 700L/700R). A tire burst or flailing tread releases debris within the wheel bay of the affected unit. Nose-unit debris acts in zone 110 (forward hull, forward avionics rack, channel-1 busbar/battery, primary sensor set). Main-unit debris acts in the nacelle (zone 700), which is a designated fire zone containing the propulsion unit, inverter, TMS radiator and HV run A/B penetration. Study at drawing/model stage — installation not frozen.
praData.systems: LDG, PRL/PRR, FCA, DPP, EL1/EL2, TMS, FPR (nacelle detection loop)
praData.csfl: Nacelle tire burst is a single physical event able to reach an HV run (R-1 in 700L / R-2 in 700R), the TMS radiator (R-4), the propulsion inverter and the nacelle fire-detection loop of ONE channel co-located in that nacelle — a candidate common cause across otherwise channel-segregated items on the struck side. Nose-unit debris in zone 110 co-locates the channel-1 busbar/battery, the primary sensor set and the FCA computer, all on route R-5.
praData.mitigation:
Bays sealed by gear doors and drained above the static waterline (SDD §5.14.5). Cross-aircraft segregation of the two HV runs and two electrical channels limits a single-nacelle burst to one side. Feather path is independent of the propulsion bus (SDD §5.1.2). Propulsion sized for continuation of the sector on one unit (SDD §5.1.3). Establish debris trajectory model and shielding acceptability at detail stage.
Proposed requirements: • The landing gear installation shall demonstrate that tire-burst debris from a main-gear unit does not defeat both the HV run and the same-nacelle fire-detection loop such that the struck-side isolation response is lost (candidate — separation/shielding, disposition required).
• The forward-hull installation shall demonstrate that nose-tire-burst debris does not simultaneously disable the channel-1 busbar, the primary sensor set and the FCA computer co-located on route R-5 in zone 110 (candidate — disposition required).
aiRequirements: The landing gear installation shall demonstrate that tire-burst debris from a main-gear unit does not defeat both the HV run and the same-nacelle fire-detection loop such that the struck-side isolation response is lost (candidate — separation/shielding, disposition required).

The forward-hull installation shall demonstrate that nose-tire-burst debris does not simultaneously disable the channel-1 busbar, the primary sensor set and the FCA computer co-located on route R-5 in zone 110 (candidate — disposition required).

praData.desc: Bird strike is a forward-facing external threat. Credible impact points on the HA-10: the flight-deck windscreen (zone 120), the wing leading edge and empennage (zone 900, high-wing with T-tail), and the propeller / nacelle inlet plane (zone 700L/700R, wing-mounted tractor units). Windscreen strike threatens the occupied flight deck and the standby display/battery installed on the right of the panel (zone 120). Wing/empennage strike threatens control runs and the water rudder (zone 900). Propeller/nacelle strike threatens a propulsion unit and its nacelle contents. Study at drawing/model stage.
praData.systems: DPS (standby display + battery, zone 120), FCA/FCB surface runs, HUA (water rudder, zone 900), PRL/PRR (propeller, zone 700)
praData.csfl: A single windscreen strike acts in zone 120, which houses BOTH pilots' primary display units and the standby display with its dedicated battery — a co-location that could couple the primary and standby indication paths despite their four-way electrical/sensor independence (SDD §5.11). Empennage/T-tail strike acts on control surface runs in zone 900 where primary control runs are present.
praData.mitigation:
Standby display independent of the primary across sensor, probe, electrical channel and battery (SDD §5.11.3) — an independence claim that a co-located flight-deck strike could still defeat physically. Channel A and B computers are separated the length of the cabin (zones 110 and 300), so neither flight-control computer is in the windscreen strike zone. Establish windscreen impact substantiation and forward-structure survivability at detail stage.
Proposed requirements: • The flight-deck installation shall demonstrate that a single bird-strike event at the windscreen does not simultaneously disable both primary display units and the standby display co-located in zone 120 (candidate — disposition required).
• The empennage installation shall demonstrate that a bird strike on the T-tail does not defeat both flight-control surface halves of any pair driven through zone 900 (candidate — disposition required).
aiRequirements: The flight-deck installation shall demonstrate that a single bird-strike event at the windscreen does not simultaneously disable both primary display units and the standby display co-located in zone 120 (candidate — disposition required).

The empennage installation shall demonstrate that a bird strike on the T-tail does not defeat both flight-control surface halves of any pair driven through zone 900 (candidate — disposition required).

praData.threat: Lightning strike (direct attachment and induced transients per §25.581/§25.1316, AC 20-136B)
praData.desc: Direct attachment to extremities (wingtips, empennage, nose, propeller/nacelle) and swept-stroke exit, with induced transients coupling into wiring bundles along the six zone-spanning routings. Because Lightning is a single external event able to reach both electrical channels and both flight-control channels simultaneously, it is a candidate common-cause contributor that can defeat the FCA/FCB independence argued on dissimilar processors, dissimilar air-data sources and left/right routing (R-5 on the left, R-6 on the right, crossing only at the flight-deck bulkhead 400 mm apart). Attachment at a wing extremity or nacelle can couple into HV run A (R-1) and HV run B (R-2), the channel-1/channel-2 electrical runs (R-5/R-6), the dual fire-detection loops (loop 1 on R-5, loop 2 on R-6) and the fuel gallery/burner region (R-3, aft fuselage fire zone, fuel present). Survivability claim to be substantiated: transient effects are MINIMISED by bonding, shielding and transient suppression such that no Catastrophic/Hazardous failure condition results from a single strike.
praData.systems: FCA, FCB, EL1, EL2, DPP, DPS, PRL, PRR, EST, EGN, FPR, LDG
praData.csfl: Common external strike coupling into both channel-1 (R-5) and channel-2 (R-6) runs simultaneously defeats the FCA/FCB independence claim (dissimilar processors, dissimilar air-data, left/right segregation) and the dual fire-loop segregation (loop 1 on R-5, loop 2 on R-6); a single event thereby reaches nominally independent redundancies and must appear as a common-cause contributor in the affected fault trees rather than be omitted.
praData.mitigation:
Bonding and grounding of the airframe and metallic components; shielding and transient suppression on the R-5/R-6 electrical runs and on the dual fire-detection loops; separation maintained at the flight-deck bulkhead (separate grommets 400 mm apart) and by left/right routing of R-1/R-5 versus R-2/R-6; firewall shutoff valve outside the aft-fuselage fire zone on the fuel gallery (R-3); insulation-monitoring device on the HV store reporting leakage to airframe. Adequacy of induced-transient levels against equipment susceptibility is to be substantiated by test/analysis, not asserted here.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft electrical and electronic installation shall be protected against direct and induced lightning effects such that no single lightning strike produces a Catastrophic or Hazardous failure condition (to be verified against §25.1316).
• The channel-1 (R-5) and channel-2 (R-6) electrical runs and the two fire-detection loops shall retain their segregation under lightning-induced transients so that a single strike does not disable both flight-control channels or both detection loops.

praData.desc: External high-intensity radiated fields coupling into electronic equipment and interconnecting wiring throughout the airframe. HIRF is an ambient field that illuminates the whole aircraft at once, so it reaches both flight-control channels, both electrical channels and both displays simultaneously and is therefore a common-cause contributor against the FCA/FCB independence argument (dissimilar processors, dissimilar air-data sources, left/right segregation on R-5/R-6). It can also couple into the crew-alerting function hosted in the display units — the single point at which all system alerts are prioritised — and into the dual fire-detection loops and the flight-control cross-compare paths. The flight-control channels each read a single-source air-data set (primary sensor set for FCA, standby set for FCB); erroneous or corrupted data induced by fields is a credible HIRF effect on those sensing chains.
praData.systems: FCA, FCB, DPP, DPS, EL1, EL2, PRL, PRR, EST, EGN, FPR, LDG, ECS
praData.csfl: Whole-aircraft field illumination reaches channel-1 (R-5) and channel-2 (R-6) equipment and both display sensor sets at once, defeating the FCA/FCB and DPP/DPS independence claims and potentially the crew-alerting prioritisation function common to both display units; this common-mode susceptibility must be reflected in the affected fault trees rather than dismissed on the strength of the logical redundancy.
praData.mitigation:
Equipment HIRF qualification and installation-level shielding of the R-5/R-6 runs and equipment enclosures; dissimilar processors and dissimilar air-data sources across FCA/FCB reduce, but do not by themselves eliminate, common-mode field susceptibility; monitored cross-compare of surface position between channels and continuous primary-versus-standby cross-comparison provide detection of induced disagreements (annunciated, not auto-resolved). Adequacy against the §25.1317 HIRF environment is to be substantiated by test/analysis at equipment and installation level, not asserted here.
Proposed requirements: • Each flight-critical electronic system and its installation shall meet its intended function and shall not produce a Catastrophic or Hazardous failure condition when exposed to the HIRF environment of §25.1317.
• The FCA/FCB and DPP/DPS independence claims shall be substantiated to hold under HIRF illumination, or the common-mode susceptibility shall be carried as a common-cause contributor in the affected fault trees.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structure and intakes (§25.571(e)(2))
praData.desc: Hail impact on forward-facing surfaces and openings: nose and forward hull (110), flight-deck windscreen (120), nacelle inlets and TMS radiators (700L/700R), and wing/empennage leading edges (900). Study is drawing/model stage — SDD §1.2 figures are preliminary and the ice/hail-impact envelope is not defined in the SDD, so airframe survivability against a defined hailstone is not substantiated here.

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding (§25.1419, AC 20-73A)
praData.desc: Ice accretion on unprotected surfaces and probes, and shed-ice impact: pitot probes and static ports (feeding primary and standby air data), windscreen (120), propeller and nacelle inlets (700L/700R), wing and empennage leading edges (900). The SDD describes heated pitot probes and bleed/electric windscreen anti-fog but does NOT describe an airframe/propeller ice-protection design, so protection adequacy cannot be grounded — refine to the type-design ice envelope. Drawing/model stage per App L.1.2.
praData.systems: DPP (two heated pitot probes), DPS (second probe), PRL/PRR (propellers, nacelle inlets, TMS radiators), ECS (windscreen anti-fog — bleed with electric backup), TMS (nacelle radiator flaps)
praData.csfl: A common icing condition acting on both pitot probes simultaneously is a shared external cause that can defeat the primary/standby air-data dissimilarity that FCA and FCB rely on; ice shed from the propellers or wing can strike the nacelle inlets/radiators (zone 700) and the empennage (zone 900).

praData.threat: Cabin fire / in-flight cabin or baggage fire and smoke (§25.831(c)/§25.855)
praData.desc: In-flight fire or smoke originating in an occupied compartment or baggage. Detection is photoelectric cabin/baggage smoke sensing reporting to the crew alerting function (separate from the fire-zone loop detectors). Survivability concern: smoke migration to the flight deck via the ECS overhead distribution ducting, and co-location of a fire in the aft cabin equipment bay (zone 300) with flight control channel B (FCC B), the channel-2 busbar and battery. Store bay (600) vents overboard and shares no ventilation path with the cabin, so a store thermal event is not a cabin-fire source. Preliminary/drawing-stage installation per SDD Issue 1.
praData.systems: FPR (cabin/baggage smoke detection), ECS (overhead distribution ducting, outflow/relief), FCB (aft cabin equipment bay, zone 300), EL2 (channel-2 busbar and battery, zone 300), DPP (crew alerting function)
praData.mitigation: Photoelectric cabin and baggage smoke detection reporting to the crew alerting function; ECS overhead distribution and outflow/relief valve for smoke removal; watertight bulkhead at frame 14 as a compartment boundary. NOTE co-location to disposition: FCC B, the channel-2 busbar and the channel-2 battery are all installed in the aft cabin equipment bay (zone 300) — a cabin/baggage fire in that zone could defeat channel-2 loads, so the channel-A/channel-B independence claim must be assessed against this common location (feed to CMA/ZSA). Separation, fire containment or relocation to be substantiated.

cmaData.subject: G-002 — SF-011-M2 store-bay detection AND alerting (page-1788206903688-142, nodes 3/6/7 under gate id 2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Loop 1 (CH1/R-5) and loop 2 (CH2/R-6) on separate electrical channels and routes; BMS module thermal sensing is a dissimilar third means; crew alerting is a further input.. Dual detection loops, module-level BMS thermal sensing and the crew alerting function fail independently, so undetected failure to warn of a store-bay event requires their coincident failure.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1. Crew alerting function shared across ALL warning branches (node 7 replicates as nodes 11/15/19 and node 20 sits directly under the top OR) | A single alerting-function failure defeats warning for every zone at once — the AND is falsely optimistic for this contributor | Alerting hosted in the primary display units on channel 1 (SDD §5.10.2); SDD flags the DPP/FCA channel-1 commonality as 'an installation item to be examined'. Belongs as a repeated event / dedicated common-cause gate, not inside the AND.
2. Both detection loops co-located within the same designated fire zone (600) | The thermal/fire event being detected is itself a shared harsh environment acting on both loops | Store bay is a designated fire zone, vented overboard; loops routed within their own zone. Common-environment coupling on the detected event.
3. Common design of the two detection loops (identical loop technology) | Common specification/manufacturing-lot fault could disable both loops | SDD asserts dual-loop AND-for-warning; dissimilarity of the two loops not stated. BMS module sensing is a dissimilar principle that partially mitigates in the store bay only.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the crew alerting function as a repeated event / common-cause gate across all warning branches rather than as an independent AND input. Preserve loop CH1/CH2 electrical-channel and R-5/R-6 route separation. Retain BMS module thermal sensing as the dissimilar third detection principle for the store bay.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The crew alerting function shall be shown independent of any single detection loop's channel, or its common-cause contribution shall be modelled explicitly in the SF-011-M2 fault tree.
• Detection loop 1 and loop 2 for the store bay shall not share electrical channel, physical route or common failure susceptibility such that a single cause disables both.

cmaData.subject: G-007 dual-principle independence — store-bay detection lost (SF-011-TL2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two dissimilar sensing principles in the store bay — dual-loop fire detection plus battery-management module-level thermal sensing — combined in an AND for loss of detection.. Store-bay detection is lost only if both loops AND the BMS module-level thermal sensing fail together.
cmaData.findings: Strong dissimilarity argument at the sensing-principle level: loop detection and BMS module thermal sensing are different means, defeating common-design/common-software coupling between them. Electrical channel separation of the two loops is credible per SDD.

Retain the two dissimilar principles as the primary independence argument. Keep the BMS thermal-event discrete on a path independent of the loop-detection annunciation where feasible. Assess the shared loop-fault annunciation / crew-alerting path as a separate common single point (already modelled at node 37).
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Store-bay loss of detection shall rely on two dissimilar sensing principles (loop detection and BMS module thermal sensing) with no shared design, software or processing element between them (independence requirement, PSSA).
• The BMS thermal-event discrete and the loop-detection warning shall reach the crew via paths whose common elements are separately assessed as single points.

cmaData.findings: Installation-design / environment common cause: both loops are co-located in the turbogenerator compartment (zone 800, designated fire zone), so a single severe zonal event (the fire itself, or a turbogenerator burst / thermal event) can defeat both loops simultaneously — unlike the store bay, this zone has no dissimilar second principle to break the coupling. Common-function single point: the crew-alerting / loop-fault annunciation path is shared (node 37/38). Loop-to-loop electrical/route separation is credible per SDD.

Retain channel/route separation of the two loops. Because there is no dissimilar second principle here, the ZSA for zone 800 must confirm that no credible single zonal source fails both loops before annunciation; consider whether a dissimilar second sensing means or a zonal-event-tolerant routing is warranted. Assess the shared annunciation path as a separate single point.

Verification (SSA/ASA): ZSA for zone 700L to be reconciled: a nacelle fire that this gate is meant to detect must not be assumed to disable both loops before annunciation.

cmaData.subject: G-014 — Generator-bay response fails (fuel shutoff and single extinguishant bottle), SF-012-M3
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dissimilar suppression response in the turbogenerator compartment: a fuel-shutoff command to the turbogenerator feed AND discharge of the single extinguishant bottle — two different mechanisms addressing one event.. The fuel-shutoff command path and the single generator-compartment extinguishant bottle fail independently (AND gate).
cmaData.findings: The two response paths are dissimilar by design (fuel isolation vs extinguishant discharge), which supports functional independence. RESIDUAL COMMON CAUSE — (1) Common command source: both the fuel-shutoff command and the extinguishant-discharge command originate from the SAME fire & thermal protection function (FPR), so an FPR command/logic failure, or the underlying loss of detection, defeats both responses together — this is the reason the parent gate G-013/node 40 is an AND with the detection path and the not-annunciated leaf. (2) Installation-Design / Environment: both the fuel-gallery firewall shutoff valve and the extinguishant bottle are in / adjacent to zone 800 (aft-fuselage fire zone); the very fire this gate responds to can damage both mechanisms before they act. (3) Suppression is NOT redundant — a single bottle with no reserve — so there is no margin within the extinguishant path itself.
cmaData.mitigation:
Dissimilarity of the two mechanisms is the primary mitigation and holds provided each is triggered independently once commanded. Independence requirement (dev): the fuel-shutoff command and the extinguishant-discharge command shall not share a single point of processing/annunciation within FPR whose failure disables both; the firewall shutoff valve is mounted OUTSIDE the fire zone per SDD, which mitigates the thermal common cause for that path. Verification note (ASA): confirm the extinguishant bottle and its actuation survive the credible generator-bay fire long enough to discharge; confirm FPR command architecture provides independent trigger paths for shutoff and discharge; confirm zone-800 zonal analysis does not credit both responses surviving the same fire.
Verification (SSA/ASA): Reconcile against zone-800 ZSA and against SF-012-M / inadvertent-discharge concern; the single-bottle, no-reserve architecture removes any suppression margin, so containment/isolation must carry the response the extinguishant cannot.

cmaData.aiVerification: Reconcile against zone-800 ZSA and against SF-012-M / inadvertent-discharge concern; the single-bottle, no-reserve architecture removes any suppression margin, so containment/isolation must carry the response the extinguishant cannot.

cmaData.subject: SF-011-TL2 top AND — detection-capability loss AND loop-fault annunciation defeated
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Detection redundancy (dual loops per zone, loop 1 on R-5/channel 1, loop 2 on R-6/channel 2) is independent of the loop-fault annunciation path.. The two branches of the SF-011-TL2 AND (detection lost across all zones; loop-fault annunciation defeated) fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence — (1) Crew alerting function is a single hosted function in the display units that prioritises all warnings | if silent, loop-fault annunciation branch (nodes 38/39) is defeated while detection is separately lost | alerting reads from every system but is one logical place — SDD flags this, no dissimilar backup annunciator stated. (2) Both detection loops share nothing above their own channel per zone, BUT channels 1 and 2 both originate at EST/DC-OR and both DC/DC converters sit in zone 600 | a store-bay event or bay-level common cause could strike both loops' power | loops route on separate R-5/R-6 runs and separate grommets 400 mm apart at flight-deck bulkhead. (3) Node 36 'Common-cause loss of both detection loops' already present in tree | correctly seeds the CCF term | verify beta/coverage in quantitative activity, not asserted here.
cmaData.mitigation: Verify the crew alerting function is not a single point that defeats both AND branches; confirm node 36 CCF term captures shared bay-level and channel-power coupling; confirm dual-loop AND-for-warning / OR-for-fault logic as built.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Detection redundancy (dual loops per zone, loop 1 on R-5/channel 1, loop 2 on R-6/channel 2) is independent of the loop-fault annunciation path.

cmaData.subject: SF-012-M3 top AND — demanded suppression/isolation response fails AND failure not annunciated
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: The suppression/isolation response paths are independent of the annunciation that the response failed.. The two branches of the SF-012-M3 AND (response fails; failure not annunciated) fail independently.
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence — (1) 'Failure of the response is not annunciated' (node 49) is the crew alerting function, the same single hosted function relied on in SF-011-TL2 | a silent alerting function defeats the annunciation branch while the response is separately lost | SDD records the alerting function as one prioritising place — no dissimilar annunciation path stated. (2) Response sub-tree spans three zones (store bay containment, generator-bay fuel-shutoff+bottle, nacelle contactor-open+feather); commands out from FPR on channels 1/2 | a common FPR command-channel or bay-level fault could couple multiple response paths | commands split loop 1/R-5 and loop 2/R-6; store response is passive containment independent of powered discharge. (3) FPR consumes EL1/EL2 both channels | loss of both LV channels defeats both response and its annunciation | diode-OR / dual-channel feed per SDD — verify no single converter/bay fault takes both.
cmaData.mitigation: Verify the crew alerting function (node 49) is not the same single element whose loss also defeats detection annunciation; confirm FPR command paths and LV feeds do not share a single defeat point across response and annunciation branches.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: The suppression/isolation response paths are independent of the annunciation that the response failed.

cmaData.subject: G-015 — Nacelle isolation response AND: propulsion-bus contactor-open command fails AND feather path fails
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Contactor-open isolation and propeller feather are independent means of achieving nacelle isolation.. The propulsion-bus contactor-open command and the feather path fail independently (nacelle isolation response AND, nodes 46/47/48).
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence — (1) Contactor-open command originates from FPR (isolation output) to the propulsion bus in zone 600 | a fault in the FPR command channel disables the contactor-open leg | contactor has its own controller reporting its own state; no two contactors share a controller. (2) Feather is documented as hydro-mechanically governed and independent of the propulsion bus, with electrical feather on command | if the feather command shares origin with the isolation command (both FPR/flight-control), a common command-channel fault could defeat both | SDD states feather does not depend on the propulsion bus, and feather is also auto-commanded by flight-control on locked-rotor — a dissimilar trigger. (3) Both propulsion-unit response elements sit in the nacelle (zone 700, designated fire zone) | the very fire/overheat event being isolated is co-located with both response actuators | isolation acts to remove energy; feather is hydro-mechanical from an engine-driven pump — verify the fire event cannot disable both before action completes.
cmaData.mitigation: Verify the contactor-open command and the feather command do not share a single command channel or power source; confirm feather's independence of the propulsion bus as built and that the nacelle fire event cannot disable both response paths before completion; confirm the locked-rotor auto-feather trigger is dissimilar to the FPR isolation trigger.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Contactor-open isolation and propeller feather are independent means of achieving nacelle isolation.
